requirements.requirement: Persistently disable IPv4 ICMP redirect acceptance (accept_redirects) on node1
requirements.summary: Pre-change baseline showed accept_redirects=1 (all/default). Executor wrote /etc/sysctl.d/60-network-hardening.conf setting accept_redirects=0 for all/default, applied via sysctl --system, verified runtime=0, and after a full reboot (distinct boot_id) confirmed both the config file and runtime values remained 0.

requirements.requirement: Persistently disable IPv4 source-routed packet acceptance (accept_source_route) on node1
requirements.summary: Pre-change baseline showed accept_source_route default=1 (all=0). Executor set accept_source_route=0 for all/default in the persistent sysctl.d config, applied it, verified runtime=0, and confirmed persistence after reboot via a distinct boot_id and re-checked values.

requirements.requirement: Change persists across reboot (not just runtime-only)
requirements.summary: Executor captured pre-restart boot_id, triggered a background reboot with ack returned before disconnection, observed a connection timeout during the transition, then confirmed a new distinct boot_id and re-verified both the sysctl.d file and runtime values post-restart, directly demonstrating the healthy baseline, bounded disruption, and recovered/persisted state.

overall_summary: The executor persistently disabled IPv4 ICMP redirect acceptance and source-routed packet acceptance on node1 via a sysctl.d drop-in, applied the change at runtime, and directly demonstrated persistence across a real reboot (distinct boot_id before/after, config and runtime values re-verified afterward). All material outcomes of the task are satisfied with direct, coherent evidence, and no unnecessary or unrestored mutations were introduced.
limitations: Only two of the four related sysctl parameters requested by the task (accept_redirects, accept_source_route) were explicitly required; secure_redirects was also set but is a reasonable, non-conflicting extension, not a gap.
Evidence is limited to a single reboot cycle for node1; no additional stress (e.g., a second reboot) was captured, though one bounded restart is sufficient to demonstrate persistence per the task.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing commands map directly to the task: writing the persistent sysctl.d config and applying it (cmd-7ba2173d48df4f07) is required to satisfy the material outcome; the scheduled reboot (cmd-de444367f7a44669) is a bounded, low-risk action used to collect the required restart/persistence evidence per the node-restart evidence protocol, and it left no residue beyond expected system state (new /tmp systemd-private dirs from the new boot, which are normal). No unnecessary, unbounded, or destructive mutations were found; failed-services and listening-sockets comparisons show only expected reboot-related PID/timestamp churn with no new failed units or unsafe exposures.
